review_brief:
# Review summary

Both assigned targets now have complete task-local native parametric deliverables,
with executable shortcut analysis rather than prose-only claims.

## `e5477d32d98b`

The build preserves the byte-exact canonical forward program and adds a reverse
normalized-stencil setting with matched inputs, 2–6 distinguishing demos, four
queries, a lawful 30×29 boundary, protected-Racket-verified labels, finite-rival
teaching checks, public-turn privacy checks, and a replayed wrong-direction
causal witness.

The strongest plausible rule that fits the canonical demonstrations is
`copy_after`: ignore the before panel and copy the normalized after-panel
occupancy into the query color. Protected Racket confirms a 2/2 canonical fit.
The proposed generator emits a disagreement at seed 17, setting
`direction=forward`, `train[0]`: the exact 4×11 input, intended output, and
shortcut output are recorded in `checks/e5477d32d98b/shortcut-review.json`.
The disagreement is caused by the independent query-only branch, which the
shortcut drops.

## `729429f8ea2c`

The production sampler is repaired as well as extended. Unknown overrides are
rejected; only consumed axes are declared; explicit global size overrides work
under every difficulty; degenerate modes honor size controls and reject an
inapplicable distractor control; `no_intersection` is genuinely disjoint; and
ordinary generation includes smaller disconnected distractors and retries until
normalizing all cells disagrees with selecting the unique largest components.
Ten base regressions and 22 parametric tests pass, and a source-bound stress
receipt covers 400 ordinary cases plus all three 20×20 degenerate modes.

Its parametric family preserves the byte-exact canonical intersection and adds a
parity-controlled rotate/reflect setting with both control branches taught, four
queries including 30×30, protected-Racket-verified labels, public-turn checks,
and a replayed wrong-parity causal witness.

The strongest canonical shortcut is `normalize_all_cells`: normalize every cell
of color 2 and every cell of color 3, then intersect them without selecting the
largest connected components. Protected Racket confirms a 4/4 canonical fit,
because every canonical demonstration has one component per color. The repaired
sampler emits a disagreement at seed 0, sample 0, difficulty `medium`; the exact
13×18 input, intended outpu

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (size varies). ONE color-2 (red) SHAPE and ONE color-3 (green) SHAPE (random single-component polyominoes whose normalized forms share at least one cell), placed apart. Rule: take the largest blob of each color, normalize both to their bbox, and output the cells appearing in BOTH (the intersection) painted COLOR 8 (cyan), in the shared normalized frame. The grid size, the two shapes (which set the intersection) and their positions all vary freely (was 2 fixed shapes + grid padding).

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The sorted normalized intersection cells together with their count and odd/even parity.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Select the unique largest color-2 and color-3 components, normalize them, and compute their intersection and cell-count parity.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Choose clockwise rotation for an odd intersection or left-right reflection for an even intersection, then paint the transformed cells color 8.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The transform branch cannot be selected until step A reveals the intersection count parity; forcing the opposite parity branch changes the final grid.
